versionRule: This is a private implementation revision, not a normative BDP identity law. Any edit to a pinned interpretation module or dependency lock requires conscious review of admission, graph shape, resolution, built-in closure, error and budget behavior. A behavior-changing interpretation revision must increment SCHEMA_GRAPH_POLICY and refresh these source pins together. A behavior-preserving edit may retain the policy only with an explicit reviewed justification. Do not blindly regenerate pins to make a failing test pass. Tests, comments and metadata pins are a review tripwire, not a runtime source-hash identity or a proof of complete transitive semantic closure.
revision2: Adds safe bound validation, dependency-load containment, built-in aggregate integrity accounting, and consistent reference-error locations. These interpretation/admission changes receive a new private identity revision even where successful structural graph output is unchanged.
metadataReview: The Read parser now projects a missing common metadata member as an empty object in returned Resource records and recursively in owned Links, and the protocol bundle admits the new metadata member and distinguishes current Read validators from legacy-compatible retained/Event record definitions. The installed schema graph indexer imports only the shared ProtocolArtifactValidationError and lossless JSON/Type conformance helpers; it does not parse Resource records or use BDP Resource schemas as graph inputs. Graph node, URI, reference, built-in, budget and refusal behavior is unchanged, so private schema-resource-index-2 is retained. This source-pin refresh records that review, not a claim that Read wire semantics are unchanged.
scope: Pins owning graph modules, artifact ingestion, lossless JSON decoder, descriptor/canonical-URI and conformance parsing modules, protocol export surface and adjacent value/schema/error helpers, normative descriptor schema, and dependency lock. Missing $schema uses the private 2020-12 default; legacy additionalItems and bare id remain opaque, with their legacy semantics unsupported. No claim that every transitive initializer or external runtime is closed.
builtinAccounting: Every build indexes the eight immutable built-ins and charges their work under the joint graph budget. The aggregate check is repeated and charged; there is no memoized global graph or runtime engine readiness claim.
